headline: Anduril, the US maker of AI-guided defense drones and systems, is expected to be valued at about $90 billion in a sale that lets employees sell their shares, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: a valuation up almost 50% in five months, but it is an expected figure from one outlet.
importance_line: Investors and defense customers see how quickly a young defense company has grown, but the figure is expected rather than final and rests on one report.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Chosunbiz, that Anduril, the US maker of AI-guided defense drones and systems co-founded by Palmer Luckey, founder of the virtual reality firm Oculus, is expected to reach a value of about $90 billion through a tender offer, a sale in which employees sell their shares at $94.80 each, up to $1.3 billion in total. The valuation is up from $61 billion in May, and the figure is described as expected rather than final.
notes: Original Bloomberg article not opened; read the Chosunbiz report that relays it.
